claims.text: The deviation is established on this trip's own trace and needs no profile evidence to get there. The GPS artifact is unbroken — 427 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 — and it measures the driven line at 54.16 km against a booked optimal of 36.0 km. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing figure, so the rounded trip_record copy of 54.2 km is not the number the threshold test runs on. The trace figure gives an excess of 18.16 km, which clears both establishment limbs: more than 0.8 km in absolute terms and 50.44% against a 20% percentage threshold.

The excess is additionally MATERIAL, which is what opens the driver-profile check. 18.16 km exceeds the 8.0 km absolute materiality limb on its own, and 50.44% also exceeds the 50% limb. This is not a lane change or a forced U-turn on a divided road: it is roughly half the optimal distance added on top of it.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is satisfied. The trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00105 and describe the same 15 July 2026 pickup, and the excess is measured from a trace that is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), so no corroboration beyond the trace is required of the rider. The burden has shifted to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause.

The driver cannot discharge that burden with his traffic excuse. He says traffic was heavy on the PIE so he used another way, but the bundle holds no traffic advisory for this trip at all: EV-ADVIS-00105-01 is MISSING, carries no payload and has weight_multiplier 0.0. Under POL-RD-13 the assertion is tested against the advisory for this trip and nothing else; with no advisory on file POL-RD-03 is unavailable, there is no exoneration and no closure-adjusted optimal route, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver names no advisory identifier, this is a gap in the bundle rather than a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction, so it does not escalate — the deviation simply stands at the measured figure and the refund runs against the booked optimal.

The driver's own counterparty statement concedes he took a different route — 'Traffic was heavy on the PIE so I used another way' — and the trace bears that out as a deliberate line rather than lane-level navigation. An admitted deliberate detour, with no advisory artifact behind the stated reason, leaves nothing for POL-RD-03 to exonerate and no field from which an amended optimal could be built.

Nothing in the chat log shifts the detour onto the rider. All three messages are inbound rider queries plus a one-line driver non-answer; neither rider message carries a waypoint_hint and neither names a road or destination. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction that identifies a place or road specifically enough to act on, corroborated by the vehicle passing within 200 m of the waypoint; there is no such instruction and no waypoint to test, so no distance is excluded from the excess. The rider's first message — 'excuse me why are we going towards the city?' — is a contemporaneous objection, not a request.

No post-booking relocation rescues the route. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, and the dropoff is the originally booked Terminal 1 Door 3. POL-RD-05 cannot be run because no amendment occurred, and the baseline remains the booked 36.0 km.

POL-RD-12 does not apply. trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null; there is no matched pooled itinerary and no co-rider pick-up or set-down to exclude. The baseline for POL-RD-01 is therefore the ordinary booked optimal of 36.0 km, not a longer matched-itinerary figure.

POL-RD-11 does not close the refund route. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so distance and time were charged on the driven distance and the rider did bear the detour on those lines. This is not an upfront-quoted trip where the loss of an unjustified detour would fall on the driver.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. It has no gap over 90 seconds (max_gap_sec 0.0), no straight-line jump over 500 m between consecutive fixes, and a sustained sampling interval of 10 seconds against the 30-second limb (c) ceiling. So POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged and the deviation does not need independent corroboration — though it has it anyway in the driver's own admitted route change.

The POL-RD-02 arithmetic on the booked optimal route is: ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 36.0 km + 0.28 x 42.0 min) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = (3.80 + 27.00 + 11.76) + 0.80 = 42.56 + 0.80 = 43.36. There is no ERP or toll line, no airport surcharge (correctly, since this trip terminates at Changi and does not originate there), no waiting fee and no promo. Charged_total is 65.13 and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0. The refund is 65.13 less 43.36 = 21.77, rounded up to 21.80 payable — 33.4% of the charge, below the 90% full-refund share.

The rider is entitled to more than that partial. The deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own evidence, and the driver profile establishes a repeat-deviation pattern on the only field POL-RD-06 permits: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 4, at or above the threshold of 3. I disclose that EV-DPROF-00105 is IMPAIRED — issue code STALE_SNAPSHOT, weight_multiplier 0.75, its snapshot taken 108 hours before filing against a 72-hour threshold — but the finding survives the discount, because 4 flags against a threshold of 3 is over the line even after down-weighting. Under POL-RD-06(b) this licenses FULL_REFUND of charged_total, 65.13, rather than the POL-RD-02 partial of 21.80, and the two figures must be stated side by side so the size of the uplift is auditable. Nothing is withheld from the uplift: there are no ERP, toll or surcharge lines for POL-RD-09 to settle separately. Under POL-RD-06(c) the case is additionally referred to driver-conduct review, which does not displace or delay the money.

No separate pass-through correction arises and none should be added on top of the distance-and-time figure. There are no erp_gantries charged and airport_surcharge is 0.0, which is right because the Changi surcharge falls only on trips originating at the airport and this trip ends there. POL-RD-09(1) is the anti-double-count rule: the POL-RD-02 refund already comprehends any off-route ERP, so the 21.80 figure must not be inflated by a second pass-through line — and on the full-refund limb there are no pass-through lines to exclude from the uplift.

The rider-history factor in POL-RD-08 does not bite. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the rider is nowhere near the 4-or-more-claims threshold that would demand corroboration beyond the trace. No profile-based discount applies to this claim. I cite only that field because POL-GEN-01 confines the rider profile to the POL-RD-08 test and makes every other field on it context only.

This case should be decided, not escalated. The deciding fact — the deviation — rests on EV-GPS-00105 at full weight; the only impaired artifact is the driver profile at weight 0.75 (STALE_SNAPSHOT), which caps confidence at 0.75, still above the 0.70 POL-RD-10(1) floor. There is no identifier mismatch (all three artifacts carry TRP-00105), no POL-RD-07 trace impairment, no timestamp running backwards, no exculpatory clause invoked by the driver against a cited artifact, and no refund above SGD 150.00. None of the POL-RD-10 triggers fires and there is no POL-RD-10(3) corroboration problem to escalate on.

The present payment state confirms the rider still carries the disputed charge: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0 on the fare breakdown, and this dispute was filed by the rider. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute leaves that 65.13 exactly where it is, so nothing short of a refund leaves the rider whole; the rider is not made whole by the charge merely standing.

claims.text: The rider asks for the entire fare, but POL-RD-02 fixes the remedy by arithmetic, not by sentiment: charged_total on EV-FARE-00105 is SGD 65.13, and the recomputed fare over the booked optimal route of 36.0 km and 42.0 min on EV-TRIP-00105 is SGD 3.80 base + 36.0 x SGD 0.75 = SGD 27.00 distance + 42.0 x SGD 0.28 = SGD 11.76 time, at the surge_multiplier of 1.0 recorded on the fare_breakdown and nowhere else, plus the SGD 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, no toll and no surcharge (the trip ends at, and does not originate at, Changi) = SGD 43.36. The refund is therefore SGD 65.13 - SGD 43.36 = SGD 21.77, payable as SGD 21.80. That, and not SGD 65.13, is the measure of this claim.

The rider's stated harm - that he nearly missed check-in - is not borne out by the record he himself supplied. The trip ended at 15:44:05 on EV-TRIP-00105, and his own chat message at 15:19:44 on EV-CHAT-00105 puts his flight at 17:15, leaving about 91 minutes between drop-off and departure. He was not, on this record, at the brink of a missed departure, and the inconvenience he describes cannot inflate the refund: POL-RD-02 makes the remedy arithmetic and traceable to the fare lines, not discretionary.

The only artifact capable of lifting the remedy from the POL-RD-02 partial to a refund of the whole fare is the driver's profile, and that artifact is impaired: EV-DPROF-00105 carries weight_multiplier 0.75 with issue code STALE_SNAPSHOT, its snapshot at 2026-07-11T08:00:00+08:00 being 108 hours before the dispute was filed against a 72-hour threshold, so its trailing-window counters may lag the driver's state at trip time. The impairment is disclosed as POL-GEN-02(1) requires and caps confidence on that artifact at 0.75 under POL-GEN-02(2). The driver submits that an uplift of this size should not rest wholly on a discounted, stale counter: the POL-RD-02 figure of SGD 21.80 is the measure the record supports, and if any uplifted figure is used it must be printed beside the POL-RD-02 figure and justified on the discounted counter.

The driver's explanation is an external traffic cause on the PIE, and the bundle holds no advisory that can test it. The driver does not assert that an advisory exists; he asserts that its absence is unresolved on this record. EV-ADVIS-00105-01 is MISSING, its payload is null and its weight_multiplier is 0.0, so it carries no fact: POL-RD-03's comparison of advisory, validity window and corridor cannot be run at all, and the driver's cause is untested rather than disproved. Because the exculpatory clause is invoked against an advisory artifact that is missing from the pool, POL-RD-10(5) is engaged, and under POL-RD-13 the missing identifier having been cited, no monetary ruling should issue: the case should go to a human reviewer with the advisory record and the contested SGD 65.13 should be held rather than refunded.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this case is decided, not escalated, and the whole contested charge of SGD 65.13 is returned to the rider.

The deviation is established on this trip's own evidence. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00105) is unbroken - 427 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gap and no jump - so it is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)-(c). POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement, so the driven line is 54.16 km against the booked optimal of 36.0 km (EV-TRIP-00105), and the rounded 54.2 km copy on the trip record is not the number tested. That is an excess of 18.16 km: 50.44% over optimal and more than 8.0 km absolute. The deviation is therefore both ESTABLISHED and MATERIAL. The rider's first burden under POL-RD-08 is met (all three artifacts carry TRP-00105 and the same 15 July 2026 pickup) and it shifts to the driver.

The driver's explanation - 'traffic was heavy on the PIE so I used another way' - cannot reduce that excess. POL-RD-13 tests such an assertion against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else, and there is none: EV-ADVIS-00105-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable, no exoneration runs and no closure-adjusted optimal can be built. The assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver names no advisory identifier, this is a gap in the bundle rather than the contradiction POL-RD-10(5) describes, so it does not escalate the case. No other exculpatory clause applies: there was no rider-requested detour (POL-RD-04 - the chat log holds only the rider's two objections and the driver's one-line non-answer, with no waypoint_hint and no road named), no pickup or dropoff amendment (POL-RD-05 - both amendment timestamps and both amended optimal fields are null), and the vehicle was RYDE_X, not pooled (POL-RD-12). The driver's own contemporaneous statement concedes he took a different route, but as it carries no weight_multiplier it is evidence of the route only and does not move the confidence cap in either direction.

On the base arithmetic (POL-RD-02), the fare over the 36.0 km / 42.0 min booked optimal is (3.80 + 27.00 + 11.76) at the surge_multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus the 0.80 platform fee = 43.36, giving charged_total 65.13 less 43.36 = 21.77, rounded up to 21.80. That POL-RD-02 figure is stated here and is printed beside the uplifted figure below; it is not the ruling.

Because the deviation is material, the driver profile is checked under POL-RD-06. EV-DPROF-00105 shows deviation_flags_90d of 4, at or above the threshold of 3, so a repeat-deviation pattern is established. That artifact is impaired: weight_multiplier 0.75, issue code STALE_SNAPSHOT (snapshot 108 hours before filing against a 72-hour threshold), so its counters may lag the driver's state at trip time, and it may not be treated as current. Even discounted, 4 flags against a threshold of 3 survives. With the deviation material and substantiated on this trip's own trace, POL-RD-06(b) lifts the remedy from the POL-RD-02 partial of 21.80 to a FULL REFUND of the whole charge, 65.13. The driver's submission that the uplift should not rest on a stale counter is answered: the clause fixes the pattern on that counter and the count clears the threshold after discounting, so the uplift stands and both figures are printed so its size is auditable. There are no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge lines for POL-RD-09 to settle separately (the zero airport surcharge is correct - the Changi surcharge falls on trips originating there, and this trip ends there), and no charge line is unsupported by the trace, so nothing is withheld from the uplift and no billing-integrity referral arises. POL-RD-06(c) adds a referral to driver-conduct review.

The rider's 'nearly missed check-in' point is not borne out (the trip ended 15:44:05 for a 17:15 flight), but it does not change the arithmetic - the refund follows from the trace, not from the inconvenience. The rider's history (deviation_claims_60d 0) does not engage the POL-RD-08 corroboration factor.

Confidence is 0.75, capped by the impaired driver profile (EV-DPROF-00105, weight 0.75, STALE_SNAPSHOT) that carries the pattern finding; that is at or above the 0.70 floor, so the case is decided rather than escalated. The monetary effect of 65.13 exceeds the 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so the ruling issues but the amount is held and the case is placed in the human queue for release rather than executed automatically.
referrals: POL-RD-06(c): refer the driver to driver-conduct review for a repeat material route deviation (deviation_flags_90d 4 against a threshold of 3). The referral does not displace or delay the monetary ruling.

POL-RD-12 does not apply. trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null; there is no matched pooled itinerary and no co-rider pick-up or set-down to exclude. The baseline for POL-RD-01 is therefore the ordinary booked optimal of 36.0 km, not a longer matched-itinerary figure.

POL-RD-11 does not close the refund route. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so distance and time were charged on the driven distance and the rider did bear the detour on those lines. This is not an upfront-quoted trip where the loss of an unjustified detour would fall on the driver.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. It has no gap over 90 seconds (max_gap_sec 0.0), no straight-line jump over 500 m between consecutive fixes, and a sustained sampling interval of 10 seconds against the 30-second limb (c) ceiling. So POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged and the deviation does not need independent corroboration — though it has it anyway in the driver's own admitted route change.

The POL-RD-02 arithmetic on the booked optimal route is: ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 36.0 km + 0.28 x 42.0 min) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = (3.80 + 27.00 + 11.76) + 0.80 = 42.56 + 0.80 = 43.36. There is no ERP or toll line, no airport surcharge (correctly, since this trip terminates at Changi and does not originate there), no waiting fee and no promo. Charged_total is 65.13 and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0. The refund is 65.13 less 43.36 = 21.77, rounded up to 21.80 payable — 33.4% of the charge, below the 90% full-refund share.

The rider is entitled to more than that partial. The deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own evidence, and the driver profile establishes a repeat-deviation pattern on the only field POL-RD-06 permits: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 4, at or above the threshold of 3. I disclose that EV-DPROF-00105 is IMPAIRED — issue code STALE_SNAPSHOT, weight_multiplier 0.75, its snapshot taken 108 hours before filing against a 72-hour threshold — but the finding survives the discount, because 4 flags against a threshold of 3 is over the line even after down-weighting. Under POL-RD-06(b) this licenses FULL_REFUND of charged_total, 65.13, rather than the POL-RD-02 partial of 21.80, and the two figures must be stated side by side so the size of the uplift is auditable. Nothing is withheld from the uplift: there are no ERP, toll or surcharge lines for POL-RD-09 to settle separately. Under POL-RD-06(c) the case is additionally referred to driver-conduct review, which does not displace or delay the money.

No separate pass-through correction arises and none should be added on top of the distance-and-time figure. There are no erp_gantries charged and airport_surcharge is 0.0, which is right because the Changi surcharge falls only on trips originating at the airport and this trip ends there. POL-RD-09(1) is the anti-double-count rule: the POL-RD-02 refund already comprehends any off-route ERP, so the 21.80 figure must not be inflated by a second pass-through line — and on the full-refund limb there are no pass-through lines to exclude from the uplift.

The rider-history factor in POL-RD-08 does not bite. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the rider is nowhere near the 4-or-more-claims threshold that would demand corroboration beyond the trace. No profile-based discount applies to this claim. I cite only that field because POL-GEN-01 confines the rider profile to the POL-RD-08 test and makes every other field on it context only.

This case should be decided, not escalated. The deciding fact — the deviation — rests on EV-GPS-00105 at full weight; the only impaired artifact is the driver profile at weight 0.75 (STALE_SNAPSHOT), which caps confidence at 0.75, still above the 0.70 POL-RD-10(1) floor. There is no identifier mismatch (all three artifacts carry TRP-00105), no POL-RD-07 trace impairment, no timestamp running backwards, no exculpatory clause invoked by the driver against a cited artifact, and no refund above SGD 150.00. None of the POL-RD-10 triggers fires and there is no POL-RD-10(3) corroboration problem to escalate on.

The present payment state confirms the rider still carries the disputed charge: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0 on the fare breakdown, and this dispute was filed by the rider. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute leaves that 65.13 exactly where it is, so nothing short of a refund leaves the rider whole; the rider is not made whole by the charge merely standing.

The rider asks for the entire fare, but POL-RD-02 fixes the remedy by arithmetic, not by sentiment: charged_total on EV-FARE-00105 is SGD 65.13, and the recomputed fare over the booked optimal route of 36.0 km and 42.0 min on EV-TRIP-00105 is SGD 3.80 base + 36.0 x SGD 0.75 = SGD 27.00 distance + 42.0 x SGD 0.28 = SGD 11.76 time, at the surge_multiplier of 1.0 recorded on the fare_breakdown and nowhere else, plus the SGD 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, no toll and no surcharge (the trip ends at, and does not originate at, Changi) = SGD 43.36. The refund is therefore SGD 65.13 - SGD 43.36 = SGD 21.77, payable as SGD 21.80. That, and not SGD 65.13, is the measure of this claim.

The rider's stated harm - that he nearly missed check-in - is not borne out by the record he himself supplied. The trip ended at 15:44:05 on EV-TRIP-00105, and his own chat message at 15:19:44 on EV-CHAT-00105 puts his flight at 17:15, leaving about 91 minutes between drop-off and departure. He was not, on this record, at the brink of a missed departure, and the inconvenience he describes cannot inflate the refund: POL-RD-02 makes the remedy arithmetic and traceable to the fare lines, not discretionary.

The only artifact capable of lifting the remedy from the POL-RD-02 partial to a refund of the whole fare is the driver's profile, and that artifact is impaired: EV-DPROF-00105 carries weight_multiplier 0.75 with issue code STALE_SNAPSHOT, its snapshot at 2026-07-11T08:00:00+08:00 being 108 hours before the dispute was filed against a 72-hour threshold, so its trailing-window counters may lag the driver's state at trip time. The impairment is disclosed as POL-GEN-02(1) requires and caps confidence on that artifact at 0.75 under POL-GEN-02(2). The driver submits that an uplift of this size should not rest wholly on a discounted, stale counter: the POL-RD-02 figure of SGD 21.80 is the measure the record supports, and if any uplifted figure is used it must be printed beside the POL-RD-02 figure and justified on the discounted counter.

The driver's explanation is an external traffic cause on the PIE, and the bundle holds no advisory that can test it. The driver does not assert that an advisory exists; he asserts that its absence is unresolved on this record. EV-ADVIS-00105-01 is MISSING, its payload is null and its weight_multiplier is 0.0, so it carries no fact: POL-RD-03's comparison of advisory, validity window and corridor cannot be run at all, and the driver's cause is untested rather than disproved. Because the exculpatory clause is invoked against an advisory artifact that is missing from the pool, POL-RD-10(5) is engaged, and under POL-RD-13 the missing identifier having been cited, no monetary ruling should issue: the case should go to a human reviewer with the advisory record and the contested SGD 65.13 should be held rather than refunded.
